scenes.say: Want your .NET code to run faster? Should you use the stack or heap for buffers?

scenes.label: Span<T>
scenes.sub: Stack-only, fast, perfect for slicing arrays.
scenes.say: Span of T is stack-only and super fast. It's perfect for slicing arrays and buffers without heap allocations.

scenes.label: Memory<T>
scenes.say: Memory of T works with async code and can cross method boundaries. It's heap-friendly when you need data to last longer.

scenes.code:
Span<byte> slice = buffer.AsSpan(10, 20);
Memory<byte> mem = new Memory<byte>(buffer, 10, 20);
scenes.say: Here's how you use them. Span for in-place processing, Memory for async APIs.

scenes.question: Can Span<T> be used in async methods?
scenes.right: Nope! Span of T is stack-only and can't cross async boundaries.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Can Span of T be used in async methods? Nope! It's stack-only and can't cross async boundaries.
